newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels seen planning massive strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels seen planning massive strike.

text.p: Colombian rebels plan to launch a huge strike to mark the first anniversary of one of the bloodiest chapters in the country's guerrilla war, military intelligence services said on Tuesday.

They said the army had intercepted a radio conversation between Manuel "Sure-Shot" Marulanda, the supreme commander of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), and Joaquin Gomez, head of the rebel force's so-called Southern Bloc.

"We intercepted a conversation between Marulanda and Gomez, and we are on alert," an army spokesman said. "We have taken measures to prevent attacks, but logically we cannot say what those measures are," he added.
Gomez, who has emerged as one of the FARC's top military strategists, ordered an attack on the Las Delicias military base in the southern province of Putumayo last August.

At least 27 soldiers died in the raid, and 60 were taken prisoner. They were released 9-1/2 months later in a public ceremony on June 15 that political analysts saw as one of the FARC's greatest political and military victories.

The army spokesman said the conversation between the two rebel commanders indicated that the FARC, set up as a pro-Soviet force in 1964, wanted to launch a similar strike against another jungle base in southern Colombia before the end of this month.
